messages:
alex: Heads up — we're seeing intermittent 502s from the cache layer when clients include debug headers and mix trailing slashes. Maybe rewrite rules are colliding. Anyone touched gateway rewrite logic recently?

maria: I added an inbound rule last week to inject X-Client-Id and strip session query params for analytics. Could be related. Which headers are showing up in the failing requests?

alex: Example failing request we captured: `GET /v1/models/?session_id=abc&debug=1` Host: api.redwood.dev  X-Debug: true  X-Forwarded-Client: client-123

jordan: If we're injecting X-Client-Id unconditionally, that changes cache-key composition. Also trailing slash vs no-trailing-slash is causing different upstream cache entries. Two separate rewrite behaviors colliding.

maria: Ah — my rule currently just does `add-header X-Client-Id from X-Forwarded-Client` with no condition. I can add an `unless header_exists X-Debug` clause.

alex: We also need to canonicalize path before cache-key/signature calc. Backend treats `/v1/models` and `/v1/models/` differently; that churns caches and confuses signed-upload flows.

sam: Important: signed uploads (S3 signed URLs) break if we reorder or normalize query params used in signature. We must not touch query order for `/signed-upload` endpoints or routes that rely on upstream signatures.

jordan: Proposal: make rewrite rules declarative and conditional. e.g. `add-header` only when `not header X-Debug` AND `skip` rewrites for routes in a preserve list. Also emit telemetry when we skip/inject.

maria: Draft config example (will open PR):
```
rewrite:
  remove_headers: [X-Debug, X-Local-Trace]
  add_headers:
    X-Client-Id: from X-Forwarded-Client
  conditions:
    - not header_exists X-Debug
path:
  normalize: remove_trailing_slash
query:
  preserve_order_for: ["/signed-upload", "/presigned/*"]
route_exceptions:
  - match: /signed-upload
    skip_rewrites: true
```

alex: That looks reasonable. Please include a telemetry tag when we skip because of `X-Debug` so we can measure how often clients rely on debug headers: `rewrite.skipped=debug_present`.

maria: good call — will add `metric: rewrite.skipped_reason` with values `debug_present|preserve_path|other` to the change.

sam: I'll add an explicit `preserve_query` flag to route config so we don't accidentally normalize order globally. Also we should add integration tests for signed URL passthrough.

jordan: Tests: assert cache-key excludes `X-Debug`, assert path normalization removes trailing slash before cache key, and assert `/signed-upload` query order preserved. I'll add unit tests for key functions.

alex: Rollout plan: canary -> 10% (eng-platform-canary) -> 50% -> global. Add monitoring alert for 5xx regression and `rewrite.skipped` spike.

maria: PR incoming today, will include config patch + metrics + docs in platform-runbook.

sam: @deploy-bot canary request: roll `gateway-rewrite-v2` to eng-platform-canary with the new rule set.

deploy-bot: rolling out `gateway-rewrite-v2` to `eng-platform-canary` (10% traffic). Monitoring hooks enabled.

maria: Canary logs so far: ~15% requests hit `skip_rewrites` condition, 0 new 5xx in the last 20m.

jordan: Nice. After tests and docs merged, let's schedule the 50% stage tomorrow morning and keep rollback button handy.

alex: I'll add the runbook entry and the dashboard tile for `rewrite.skipped_reason` and `rewrite.error_rate`. Thanks all.

maria: :thumbsup: will follow up with PR link here when ready.

sam: Also noting: update integration with edge-caching team so their cache-key generation uses the normalized path field rather than raw request path.

jordan: cool — I'll ping them in #eng-runtime and share the test vectors.

alex: End of thread for now. Thanks — tracking in the PR.
